message.content:
Here’s a quick reference to the Canadian federal holidays that create **long weekends** in 2023.  
(If a holiday falls on a weekday, the adjacent weekend days form a three‑day break. If it falls on a weekend, the following Monday is usually observed as the day off, extending the weekend.)

| Holiday | Date (2023) | Weekend Days Included |
|---------|-------------|-----------------------|
| **New Year’s Day** | Sunday, Jan 1 | Sat 30 Dec 2022 – Mon 1 Jan 2023 |
| **Family Day** *(BC, AB, MB, ON, SK)* | Monday, Feb 20 | Sat 18 Feb – Mon 20 Feb |
| **Good Friday** | Friday, Apr 7 | Fri 7 Apr – Sun 9 Apr |
| **Victoria Day** | Monday, May 22 | Sat 20 May – Mon 22 May |
| **Canada Day** | Saturday, Jul 1 | Sat 1 Jul – Mon 3 Jul (observed) |
| **Labour Day** | Monday, Sep 4 | Sat 2 Sep – Mon 4 Sep |
| **Thanksgiving** | Monday, Oct 9 | Sat 7 Oct – Mon 9 Oct |
| **Christmas Day** | Monday, Dec 25 | Sat 23 Dec – Mon 25 Dec |

> **Notes**
> - **Remembrance Day** (Thu Nov 11) is a statutory holiday but does *not* create a long weekend unless observed on Friday in certain provinces.
> - Some provinces have additional holidays (e.g., St. Patrick’s Day in Ontario, St. John’s Day in Newfoundland & Labrador) that may also generate long weekends. Check your specific province for those dates.

Feel free to plug this table into your holiday‑planning app!
